title: Evaluate the inner value
text: First, calculate the inner value: what is $$\sin\left(\frac{4\pi}{3}\right)?$$

subHints.title: Identify the quadrant
subHints.text: Observe that $$\frac{4\pi}{3}=\pi+\frac{\pi}{3},$$ which is in the third quadrant.

subHints.title: Remember the range
subHints.text: The output of $$\arcsin$$ must be in the principal range $$\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right].$$ $$\frac{4\pi}{3}$$ is outside this range.

subHints.title: Connection to the unit circle
subHints.text: Recall that $$\sin\left(\frac{4\pi}{3}\right)$$ represents the $$y-$$ coordinate of the point on the unit circle at the angle $$\frac{4\pi}{3}.$$

subHints.title: Find equivalent angle geometrically
subHints.text: The principal range of $$\arcsin$$ is $$\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right], $$ which is the right half of the unit circle. To find an angle in this range with the same $$y-$$ coordinate as $$\frac{4\pi}{3}, $$ imagine drawing a horizontal line straight across from Quadrant III into Quadrant IV. This line hits the right half of the circle at $$\frac{-\pi}{3}.$$\n##figure1.gif##

subHints.title: Find equivalent angle algebraically
subHints.text: We can also solve this algebraically. The angle $$\frac{4\pi}{3}$$ has a reference angle of $$\frac{\pi}{3}$$ and lies in Quadrant III, where sine is negative. In our principal range, sine is only negative in Quadrant IV. The corresponding angle in Quadrant IV is $$-\frac{\pi}{3}.$$
